items.title: Server Components and 'use client'
items.body: In the App Router, components are Server Components by default: they render on the server, can read data directly, and ship no JavaScript of their own. A 'use client' directive marks a boundary; that module and everything it imports join the client bundle.
items.question: Where should 'use client' go in a page that has a single interactive button?
items.answer: In the small button component only, not the page. Keep data fetching and static markup in Server Components and pass serializable props, or server-rendered children, into the client leaf.

items.title: Server Actions are public endpoints
items.question: Why must every Server Action re-check authentication and authorization, even if it is only rendered on an admin page?
items.answer: A Server Action is exposed as an HTTP endpoint that any client can call with crafted arguments; hiding the button protects nothing. Treat arguments as untrusted input, validate them, and verify the session and permissions inside the action itself.

items.title: NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables
items.body: Only environment variables prefixed with NEXT_PUBLIC_ are exposed to the browser, and their values are inlined into the JavaScript bundle at build time. Changing them requires a rebuild, and anything with that prefix is public.

items.title: Hydration mismatch
items.question: A component renders new Date().toLocaleTimeString() and the console reports a hydration mismatch. What is happening and how do you fix it?
items.answer: The server rendered one time string and the client's first render produced another, so the HTML does not match what React expects while hydrating. Render time- or browser-dependent values after mount (state set in useEffect), pass a fixed value from the server, or use suppressHydrationWarning for unavoidable text differences.

items.title: Keeping server code out of bundles
items.question: A client component imports a helper from lib/db.ts, which also reads process.env.DB_PASSWORD. What are the risks, and how do you turn this into a build error?
items.answer: The module is pulled into the browser bundle: non-public env vars become undefined so it breaks, and server logic or anything accidentally inlined could be exposed. Add import 'server-only' at the top of server modules so that importing them from client code fails the build.

items.title: Props crossing the boundary
items.body: Props passed from a Server Component to a Client Component must be serializable by React: primitives, plain objects, arrays, Dates, Maps, Sets, promises and similar, but not ordinary functions or class instances. Server Actions are the exception for functions.
